item.title: Entering Fall - and other Seasons
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: If it’s Tuesday, it’s Fall! With the conditions of the world (and, at least for me, money being a bit tight), I’m feeling some stress. With new seasons, we’re always trying to make our way through (this seems even more true this year). Maybe you can identify with some of the ways I’m trying to make it through this season: Here are some of my more recent seasons: Not fun seasons.

item.title: Mindfulness and mindfulness meditation
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: How much do I need to meditate to be mindful? This question lies at a modern fallacy: How little can I do something to enjoy it’s benefits? We have become used to getting things for free and as a commodity. Alas, mindfulness and meditation are inseparable. You have to meditate to be mindful. And, its not a superpower that comes with a purchase, in an app, or available without practice.

item.title: The power of silencing Notifications
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: During a meditation today, right when I was getting into my space of mental clarity, a notification came through. It’s good online meeting etiquette to mute ourselves when we join meetings, unless you’re hosting the meeting. But, we might also take the next step and turn off our notifications. If you’re on iOS (Apple) these are found under your Focus settings. Don’t be like me. Avoid interruptions right when you get into the Zone.

item.title: Just sitting there is not meditating
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description:
Just sitting there is not meditating.

I know. I’ve excused my sitting there countless times so I could cross off that day’s meditation. Our penchant for checking off items from our lists is fascinating. In reality, I could have been excused truly wanting to be with what was real and then whatever happened, happened.

item.title: Meditations per Hour (MPH) or Meditation ROI?
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: If you have a goal for meditation, make sure it’s not MPH (Meditations per Hour) but M-ROI.

item.title: Deep Dive: Lots more than I could put in a title
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: This week we look at psychological well-being - including from the U.S. Surgeon General, paying attention to the experience of detransitioners, exposomics, silence and epigenetics, Buddhism (religion or not), and my bone to pick with the Humanist Chaplaincy Network (I’m not picking any bones with humanist chaplains).

item.title: Deep Dive: Articles on contemplative practices and near death experiences
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: This week we consider recent research on mindfulness showing distinct patterns of contemplative practive help well-being. We also look at an article on the death experience during CPR. Maybe we shouldn’t blow off those near-death experiences so quickly.

item.title: Deep Dive: PTSD; nature; wanting; meditation; COVID impact; expensive cars
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: Nurses protest use of AI; the importance of personal and cultural reconsideration on the importance of sleep; prosecution of medical errors; and Zionism and the Passover.
